title: Choose the visual world for FE Café
question: The roll assigned the Risograph Study Zine. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Risograph Study Zine
options.lineage: DIY riso-printed zines and student planners
options.thesis: Every study day is a fresh hand-printed zine page, in spot inks that overprint into new colors.
materials: planner grid paper and date stamps
options.viewport: A planner spread: huge overprinted date and exam countdown on the left, today's one problem printed big on the right, with a riso-printed engraving and one obvious Start button.
options.risk: Can tip into a design-student poster if the inks are timid or the type is too clever to read.

raised.raise: One charged focal point per viewport: today's problem sits alone with real empty paper around it.
The day arrives folded: one pull opens the packet into the whole spread.
Hard ink limit: each page prints in three inks at most, and rank comes from overprint, never extra colors.
The Pomodoro runs as timed stations, each one printed as its own pass.
One motion grammar: every change registers in like a print pass, on a beat.
Today is linear: warm-up, problem, focus, log. The next step is always the obvious one.

options.label: Collectible Study Cards
options.lineage: illustrated trading cards and sticker binders
options.thesis: Each day deals you a hand of collectible cards: MAIN problem, SIDE focus session, BONUS streak.
materials: thick card stock with rounded frames
options.viewport: Three big cards dealt across a colored felt table, today's MAIN card face-up and glowing.
options.risk: Familiar: this is close to where most cozy study apps land, and it can feel like a game skin over a dashboard.

options.label: Rubber-Hose Cartoon Cel
options.thesis: Study scenes arrive through an iris, like gags in an old cartoon.
options.viewport: A round iris opening on today's problem in black-and-white cartoon ink.
options.risk: Black, white and gray only: the opposite of the color you asked for.
options.case: Fun characters, but it loses on color and on clarity for dense code.
options.kept: One motion grammar on a beat.

options.label: Ikebana Alcove
options.thesis: One branch, charged emptiness: the day as a single calm arrangement.
options.viewport: One problem off-center in a pale alcove.
options.risk: Too quiet and too far from your world of characters and color.
options.case: Great for focus, but you wouldn't recognize yourself in it.
options.kept: One charged focal point per viewport.

options.label: Miura-Fold Sheet
options.thesis: A tiny packet that unfolds into the whole study plan.
options.viewport: A gold packet that opens into a creased field of tasks.
options.case: Strong reveal mechanic, weak warmth and identification.
options.kept: The day arrives folded and opens in one pull.

options.label: Depot Destination Blind
options.thesis: Status that steps one course at a time under a fixed window.
options.viewport: A cloth roll stepping to today's task.
options.risk: A monitoring wall, not a cozy study space.
options.case: Disciplined, but built for watching systems, not learning.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Answers develop slowly under amber light.
options.viewport: A developing tray where the answer emerges.
options.risk: Dark and moody, which you said feels wrong.

options.label: Shareware Installer
options.thesis: Your study day as a Next > Next > Finish wizard.
options.viewport: A gray dialog with a pixel banner and a progress bar.
options.kept: A linear day with an obvious next step.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean study dashboard, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, streak tile, today's problem card, timer card, calendar card.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other study app, which is the template feel you asked to avoid.
